title: Self-supervised learning
reading: The slide introduces self-supervised learning as the idea of using the data itself as the supervisory signal, rather than external labels. It lists example pretext tasks posed as questions: predicting the data itself (reconstruction), predicting the rotation applied to an image, and solving a jigsaw puzzle of shuffled image patches, with an ellipsis indicating other variants. It then states the goal of these tasks: to learn representations from large-scale unlabeled data and, specifically, to learn high-level semantic representations.

concepts.name: Self-supervised learning
concepts.why_it_matters: Supervision derived from the data itself lets models exploit large unlabeled corpora.

concepts.name: Pretext tasks (reconstruction, rotation prediction, jigsaw)
concepts.why_it_matters: Concrete surrogate objectives that force a network to learn useful structure.

concepts.name: High-level semantic representations
